title: Unsynchronized Shared State Concurrency (Data Race)
damaged_code:
```scheme
;; Scheme
(define x 10)
(parallel-execute (lambda () (set! x (* x x)))
                  (lambda () (set! x (+ x 1))))
;; Interleaved execution can result in x = 11, 101, 121, etc.
```
pattern: Two concurrent processes/threads read and write a shared variable without synchronization or serialization.
why_bad: The processes interleave their read-compute-write cycles arbitrarily, corrupting the shared state (e.g., losing increments or withdrawals).
detection: Multiple concurrent threads/callbacks writing to the same memory location or shared struct field without synchronization primitives (like Mutex, Semaphore, or Atomic).
counterexample: Read-only access to shared immutable data.
fix: Wrap state mutations in serializing wrappers or acquire exclusive locks to guarantee atomic execution of critical sections.
source: Abelson & Sussman, *Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs* / passage [123, 412, 413].
